label: ESSENCE_5, essential truth: it lies in the nature of x that φ (Fine's box-sub-x), a primitive
term: essential truth of a being (ESSENCE_5; the Essential parameter)
definition: EssentialTruth Essential x φ := Essential x φ, for a being x and a world-proposition φ over the frame's points: it lies in the nature of x that φ (Fine's □ₓ φ). A parameter wrapper over the primitive Lean parameter Essential of type B → (W → Prop) → Prop of TruthCore.Modal.ModalGrounding, constrained only by the premises that use it: essence grounds necessity (EssenceGroundsNecessity: an essential truth holds at every accessible world), the essentialist account of possibility (EssentialExclusionAccount), existence-conditional essences (ExistenceConditionalEssences: every essential truth about x holds wherever x is absent) and unconditional essentialism's reading of esse = essence (EsseEssenceIsEssentialExistence). A related helper is defined: EntailsExistence F φ x, φ entails x's existence over every point of the frame's world type. Sense ESSENCE_5 of DISAMB-ESSENCE.
note: Stipulated for #1887 (docs/notes/modal-grounding-frameworks.md). Distinct from the existing EssenceReasonSeparation.Profile.InEssence, which represents only existence facts in essences and so cannot state an existence-conditional essence; the two are not related by any bridge. The other senses of DISAMB-ESSENCE (Scott, Godel, the q.3 a.4 represented essence essenceOf) are different notions: here essenceOf/esseOf remain the q.3 a.4 represented essence and esse (ESSENCE_3), and Essential is the Finean nature-relative truth; the only bridge between them is the explicit OPEN premise EsseEssenceIsEssentialExistence, listed as a sense bridge in the argument that uses both. Whether an esse-essence identity is a case of existence belonging to an essence (the Kant-type thesis) decides between controls laws 3-4 (existence-conditional essentialism makes the identity modally idle) and the unconditional-essentialist support for B6; it is open. What would source it: Fine, 'Essence and Modality' (1994); Lowe, 'Two Notions of Being' (2008).

formal_gap.meaning: EssentialTruth Essential x φ says that it lies in the nature of x that φ holds, for a proposition φ over the frame's points. A model supplies the relation; Lean fixes only its type.
examples: It lies in the nature of a singleton that it has its member.
It lies in the nature of water that it is H2O.
exclusions: Necessity: that Socrates is a member of his singleton is necessary but does not lie in Socrates' nature (Fine 1994, navigation only); essence implies necessity only under the explicit premise EssenceGroundsNecessity.
The q.3 a.4 represented essence essenceOf (ESSENCE_3): related only by the explicit premise EsseEssenceIsEssentialExistence.
A contingent being's happening to exist at w.
open_obligations: No structural property (closure under entailment, conjunction, transitivity) is assumed.
Whether essential truths are world-propositions over the frame's points.
Whether existence can belong to an essence, in particular for an esse-essence identity.
